references.text: Jesus' answer to the question about freedom: 'If the Son sets you free, you will be truly free,' which directly resolves the issue of slavery to sin in the previous verse.
Paul uses the same image of becoming 'servants' (slaves) either to sin leading to death or to obedience leading to righteousness, and confirms that one cannot serve two masters.
Paul urges believers to stand firm in the freedom Christ has given and warns against letting themselves be suffocated again under a 'yoke of slavery,' which mirrors Jesus' claim that sin is a yoke.
The text explains that our old self was crucified so that 'we should no longer be slaves to sin,' and that whoever has died is freed from sin.
